feasibility.verdict: Partially feasible: precipitation partitioning into runoff, ET, and recharge can be simulated and internally closed via ELM water-balance diagnostics; SWE, water-table depth, and streamflow (as a proxy for basin runoff) can be validated against observations, but ET has no direct observational constraint (no flux towers in domain).
answerable: Long-term mean partitioning of precipitation into runoff (QOVER+QDRAI), ET, and recharge (QCHARGE) at columns spanning the Naches elevation and soil-texture gradient
Elevation and soil-texture controls on partitioning (contrast high snow-dominated vs low rain-dominated columns)
Validation of snow (SWE) against 6 SNOTEL stations
Validation of water-table depth against USGS wells (via ELM ZWT)
Qualitative validation of runoff timing/magnitude against USGS stream gauges (recognizing scale mismatch between point column and gauged catchment)
not_answerable: Direct validation of ET (no flux-tower LE/H observations in domain)
Fully spatially distributed basin water budget or lateral routing (single-column ELM has no inter-column lateral flow; stream gauge comparison is only approximate)
Deep bedrock/regional groundwater recharge beyond ELM's soil-column bottom flux

parsed.n_justification: Six columns span the 352-1977 m elevation gradient (the dominant control on rain-vs-snow partitioning) and align with the 6 SNOTEL SWE stations for snow validation, while sampling contrasting soil textures. This is the minimum set that resolves low-elevation rain-dominated, mid-elevation transitional, and high-elevation snow-dominated regimes for a robust site-archetype partitioning analysis without redundant columns.
requires_capabilities: ELM single-column (PTS_MODE) with SNICAR snow physics for SWE
ELM variable-saturation soil hydrology with aquifer/ZWT (QCHARGE) for recharge diagnostics
GSWP3 or Daymet 1980-2018 atmospheric forcing downscaled to column lat/lon and elevation-corrected
SNOTEL SWE, USGS well WTD, and USGS daily streamflow data access for validation
Optional PFLOTRAN coupling to refine deep recharge / saturated-zone response below ELM soil column
assumptions: Spin-up of 200+ years (accelerated + final) precedes the 1980-2018 transient run to equilibrate soil moisture, snow, and water table; STOP_N=39 years covers the analysis period.
Streamflow validation is interpreted at long-term-mean and seasonal-cycle level only, since single-column runoff cannot represent routed catchment discharge or scale.
ET validation is indirect via water-balance closure (P = ET + Runoff + dStorage + Recharge) rather than flux-tower comparison, given no towers exist.
Soil textures assigned per column from SSURGO/gridded soil data; where uncertain, defaults reflect glacial/volcanic Cascade soils.
Recharge is defined as ELM QCHARGE (flux to the unconfined aquifer store); deep regional groundwater is out of scope without PFLOTRAN coupling.
Forcing is elevation-lapse-corrected to each column to preserve the rain/snow transition that drives partitioning.
